name: Code Mycelial Network Specification
synopsis: Code Mycelial Network (CMN) specification — normative documents, JSON schemas, and conformance test vectors for sovereign code distribution
intent: Provide the complete normative specification for the Code Mycelial Network protocol — seven chapters covering Substrate (discovery & identity), Mycelium (domain manifest), Spore (package format), Taste (safety evaluation), Strain (conventions), URI (addressing), and Algorithm Registry

Ship machine-readable JSON Schema definitions (cmn.json, mycelium.json, spore-core.json, spore.json, taste.json) for validating all protocol artifacts, plus conformance test vectors (merkle, signature, uri, capsule, taste gating, key rotation, bond traversal) so implementers can verify correctness without reading prose
mutations: Require verifiers to judge retired keys by the content's declared signing time (updated_at_epoch_ms, tasted_at_epoch_ms for taste), reject retired keys when it cannot be determined, make the retirement cutoff inclusive, and state that compromise requires revoked
Add 01-substrate §5.3 fixing the priority key order of published cmn.json, spore.json, mycelium.json, spore.core.json and taste.json while signing keeps JCS
Make the mycelium endpoint's primary hash authoritative for domain metadata and reserve hashes for overflow shards
Make core.key optional in spore.core.json and mycelium drafts, filled at release; still required in published spore.json replicates whose hosting domain differs from core.domain
Allow absorbed_from to be authored in spore.core.json (only spawned_from stays forbidden) and document the bond with field
Add signed capsule and key rotation conformance vectors, extend the mycelium vectors, and add manifest and spore.core consistency checks
Fix example responses to use kind: result, add the blob_tree_blake3_nfc glossary entry, and mark example keys and signatures as placeholders
